_meta: AF/G.23 round (2026-08-13). Botswana municipal/district-fiscal-tier follow-up, raw findings at /tmp/rc-research/botswana.txt. Botswana's strongest find this round is the 'higher tier of government reporting on named lower-tier units' pattern already established for Nigeria/Ethiopia: the Auditor-General's own annual reports enumerate all sixteen Town/City and District Councils by name and audit their accounts under a specific statutory mandate (Local Government Act, 2012, s.68(3)). The national Budget Speech separately confirms the 'Revenue Support Grant to District and Urban Councils' mechanism exists and is large (P5.19 billion, 55.5% of the Ministry of Local Government's recurrent budget) but does not itemize it per council or state a formula -- no single document bridges 'formula + named council + amount' the way some other countries' finds did this branch; that gap is recorded honestly in _dropped rather than forced. Two further findings enrich the existing bw-cpi-social-protection.json node bw-statsbots-cpi-technical-report-2018 (see UPDATE marker there) rather than warranting new nodes. No council (e.g. Gaborone City Council) was found to publish its own budget/financial-statement document accessibly online this session.

reports.title: Local Government Act, 2012 (Act No. 18 of 2012, Cap 40:01)
reports.description: Botswana's organic law establishing Councils' revenue base and the Auditor-General's mandate to audit them. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Section 64 (Part X, 'Revenues of Councils, Accounts and Audits') states: 'The revenues of a Council shall consist of - ... (h) the grants as the Government may make to the Council'. Section 68(3) states: '[t]he accounts under subsection (2)... shall be audited by the Auditor General' -- the exact provision the Auditor-General's own reports cite as their mandate to name and audit all Town/City and District Councils (see bw-auditor-general-report-2018-2019 and bw-auditor-general-report-2019-2020). A separate provision (Part V, Rating) states: 'It shall be lawful for the Minister in his or her discretion to make a grant to the revenue of the Council in lieu of an owner's rate, on property vested in Government... not exceeding the amount which would have been payable except for the provisions of subsection 4 (a) and (c)' -- the exact statutory mechanism behind the Auditor-General's finding of a P23,246,480 unpaid grant-in-lieu-of-rates to Gaborone City Council. Hosted on botswanalaws.com, a private Botswana legal-database mirror, not gov.bw directly; treated as adequate per this branch's established sourcing precedent for verbatim government Act text. Supersedes the pre-2012 Local Government (District Councils) Act, Cap 40:01, whose section 44 carried the same revenue-list wording ('such grants as the Government may make to the council') under older section numbering -- the predecessor was not independently minted as a corpus node since current Auditor-General reports cite the 2012 Act's section numbering, not the older instrument's.

reports.title: 2024/2025 Budget Speech
reports.description: Botswana's national budget speech, delivered by Peggy O. Serame, Minister of Finance, 5 February 2024. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Paragraph 99 (p.29): 'Mr. Speaker, Revenue Support Grants to District and Urban Councils constitute the largest portion of the Ministry's projected Recurrent Budget, amounting to five billion, one hundred and ninety million Pula (P5.19 billion) or 55.5 percent of the total budget.' This confirms the operative name and scale of the national-to-council transfer mechanism ('Revenue Support Grant', not the 'District Development Fund' name hypothesized going into this round's search -- that specific name does not appear to be the current Botswana instrument; see _dropped). The speech gives only this single aggregate figure: it does not break the P5.19 billion down by individual named council, and no allocation formula is stated anywhere in the document. Paragraph 98 (p.28-29) adds: 'Nine hundred and twenty-four million Pula (P924 million) of this budget is allocated for Councillors termination benefits, the operational expenses of upgrading Sub-Districts into fully-fledged Districts, and the projected growth in the number of Council Members and Council Wards...', confirming an active sub-district-to-district upgrading process. Hosted on bankofbotswana.bw (a mirror), not the Ministry of Finance's own site, but is unambiguously the Minister of Finance's own budget speech text.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget speech, delivered each February by the Minister of Finance to the National Assembly.

reports.title: National Development Plan 11 (2017-2023)
reports.description: Botswana's national development plan, containing a structural table mapping every Town/City/District Council to its constituent Sub-Districts and population. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. 'Table 1.1: District/City/Town Councils, Sub-Districts and Population' lists, verbatim in part: 'Gaborone City Council N/A 231 592; Francistown City Council N/A 98 961; ... Central District Council Bobirwa, Boteti, Mahalapye, Serowe/Palapye, Tutume, and Tonota 576 064; ... Chobe District N/A 23 347. Sources: Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development and 2011 Population and Housing Census'. The table is population-only and cites no budget/grant figures per council; it is useful as a structural/institutional map of which sub-districts fall under which council and as an example of a national planning document naming the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development and the 2011 Census as its data sources. Hosted on botswana.un.org (a UN country-office mirror), not npc.gov.bw directly, though described throughout as the government's own National Development Plan. A separate table-of-contents entry for a 'Local Government Infrastructure Investment and Services' section (nominal p.21 of that chapter) did not have corresponding extractable body text with named-council financial figures in the copy fetched this session.

dependencies.basis: The report states its own audit mandate directly from the statute: 'In terms of Section 68 (3) of the Local Government Act, (Cap 40:01)... I am required to audit the accounts of all Councils and Land Boards.' Section 68(3) of the Act itself states 'the accounts... shall be audited by the Auditor General' -- a direct, named statutory basis for the audit, not a general institutional mention.
dependencies.evidence_quote: 1 b) I am also required by the terms of Section 68 (3) of the Local Government Act, and Section 32 (3) of the Tribal Land Regulations to audit the accounts of the local authorities (city councils, town councils, township authorities and district councils) and land boards, and submit my reports thereon together with the audited statements to the Chief Executive Officers of these entities, who shall cause them to be laid before their respective Authorities and Boards, as the case may be.

dependencies.basis: Statistics Botswana's own Technical Report states (p.8): 'Botswana has adopted the domestic concept in-line with requirement of the Harmonized Consumer Price index (HCPI) and its providing monthly HCPI data to SADC Secretariat... HCPI is an initiative of the SADC secretariat adopted in August 2011.' This is the national-side counterpart to the existing sadc-hcpi-newsletter -> bw-statsbots-cpi edge (af-sadc-hub.json, uses_data_from), which previously had only SADC-side evidence naming Botswana; here Botswana's own document states it aligned its domestic CPI concept to the SADC HCPI framework's requirement.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Botswana has adopted the domestic concept in-line with requirement of the Harmonized Consumer Price index (HCPI) and its providing monthly HCPI data to SADC Secretariat... HCPI is an initiative of the SADC secretariat adopted in August 2011.

dependencies.basis: SELF-DECLARED: Statistics Botswana's own Technical Report states (p.32): 'Statistics Botswana CPI is currently Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) compliant in accordance with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) requirements.' Same claim shape as the existing za-statssa-cpi -> imf-sdds edge (za-fiscal-federalism.json), which used methodology_depends_on for the identical 'complies with the IMF SDDS' pattern. CAVEAT: this quote is dated December 2018 (eight years old as of this 2026 research date), so it evidences a point-in-time SDDS claim rather than confirmed current 2026 status. || SWEPT 2026-09-07 (round 7, the IMF tier sweep) and the caveat is now sharper than 'eight years old'. Botswana is not on the IMF's SDDS list (49 countries) and is not on the SDDS Plus list (32); it is an e-GDDS participant, NSDP first posted 2016-01-29 — i.e. Botswana was ALREADY an e-GDDS participant two years before this Technical Report called the CPI 'SDDS compliant'. The edge stands: Statistics Botswana's own document says its CPI meets the SDDS requirements, which is a methodology claim about the CPI and not a claim of subscription, and this corpus grades what the document says. But nothing here evidences Botswana subscribing to the SDDS, and the e-GDDS edge Botswana should carry is unminted for want of an institutional Statistics Botswana node; see int-imf-tier-sweep-2026-09-07.json.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Statistics Botswana CPI is currently Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) compliant in accordance with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) requirements.

_dropped.why: The 2024 Budget Speech states only the aggregate figure (P5.19 billion, 55.5% of the Ministry's recurrent budget) with no per-council table or stated allocation formula. The Ministry of Finance's own 'Revenues' page (finance.gov.bw) was fetched successfully and confirmed to contain no mention of Revenue Support Grant, District Development Fund, or any allocation formula. A targeted search for 'Revenue Support Grant formula' turned up no Ministry of Finance circular or subsidiary legislation. Genuine content absence in every document actually accessed, not a technical failure -- Botswana's fiscal-transfer mechanism to councils is confirmed to exist and be large, but no single accessible document bridges 'formula + named council + amount'.

The dispatch brief's hypothesized name for Botswana's national-to-council transfer mechanism does not appear to be the operative one. 'Revenue Support Grant to District and Urban Councils' is the actual, currently-used name (see bw-budget-speech-2024). Searches for a Botswana-specific 'District Development Fund' surfaced only Zimbabwe's unrelated District Development Fund Act.

_dropped.edge: Gaborone City Council's own budget/financial-statement publication
_dropped.why: No council (Gaborone City Council or otherwise) was found to publish its own budget or financial-statement document accessibly online this session. Gaborone City Council's own likely domains failed at the network level (https://www.gcc.gov.bw and https://www.gaborone.gov.bw both returned proxy CONNECT tunnel failures/HTTP 502; http://www.gaboronecitycouncil.gov.bw failed DNS resolution). Web search for 'Gaborone City Council annual financial statements report pdf' surfaced only secondary sources (Daily News, Mmegi Online, Guardian Sun, a Facebook page, directory-listing sites) -- none a primary GCC-authored budget/financial-statement document. Mixed cause: partial technical access failure on the most likely direct-domain guesses, combined with a genuine absence of any GCC-published financial-statement PDF elsewhere in the indexed web at the time of search.

A specific URL (gov.bw, 2026-06 upload folder, 'REPORT OF THE AUDITOR GENERAL... FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 MARCH 2023') appeared repeatedly and consistently across multiple independent search queries, but every direct fetch attempt (WebFetch and curl, including with a browser-like User-Agent, tried twice) returned a reproducible HTTP 404 ('Page not found | Government of Botswana'). No working URL for any Auditor-General report covering a fiscal year after March 2020 was located. Worth a future retry with different fetch tooling/timing, since the URL's consistent appearance in search results suggests it may exist but be temporarily or intermittently unavailable.
